draft.text: You came in because you have been feeling numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks.
This started after a car wreck in December when you broke both wrists.
You also have mild stiffness in your neck, which was diagnosed as a contusion.
You have not had any imaging studies for your neck or wrists since the accident.
You are willing to have an MRI of the cervical spine and X-rays of the wrists to check for nerve compression or spinal issues.
The numbness and tingling may be related to nerve compression or cervical radiculopathy.
You are also open to having electromyography (EMG) or nerve conduction studies to check for peripheral nerve involvement.
The next steps will be discussed.
You are willing to have further tests to evaluate your condition.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been feeling numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks.
This started after a car wreck in December when you broke both wrists.
You said the numbness and tingling have gotten worse over the last month.
You also have mild stiffness in your neck, which was diagnosed as a contusion.
The numbness and tingling are more noticeable in your right hand, affecting your middle and ring fingers up to your forearm.
On your left hand, it is more on your pinky and ring finger.
You are willing to have MRI and X-rays of your cervical spine and wrists to check for nerve compression or spinal issues.
You will also have electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies (NCV) to check for nerve problems or cervical radiculopathy.
